title: Realize a prescribed logarithmic lattice as an etale chart
statement:
Let $f:(X,M)\to(Y,N)$ be a morphism of locally Noetherian fs log schemes [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], log smooth in the chart sense of [def-per-fs-log-smooth-etale]. Fix a chart $Q\to N$ on $Y$, where $Q$ is fine saturated and $Q^{\rm gp}$ is torsion-free. Fix a geometric point $\bar x$ of $X$, set $A=\mathcal O_{X,\bar x}$ and $B=M_{\bar x}^{\rm gp}$, and regard $A^\times$ as a subgroup of $B$ [def-trf-fs-log-blowup, def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. The relative logarithmic differential module $\omega_{f,\bar x}$ means the $A$-module generated by $da$ for $a\in A$ and $d\log m$ for $m\in M_{\bar x}$, subject to additivity and the Leibniz rule for $d$, $dc=0$ for elements $c$ from the geometric local ring of $Y$, $d\log(mm^{\prime})=d\log m+d\log m^{\prime}$, $d\alpha(m)=\alpha(m)d\log m$, and $d\log f^\flat(b)=0$ for $b\in N_{f(\bar x)}$. Suppose $r\geq0$, $t_1,\ldots,t_r\in M_{\bar x}$, and $n\geq1$ invertible in $A$ are given such that $(d\log t_i)$ is an $A$-basis of $\omega_{f,\bar x}$. Set $L=\mathbf Z^r\oplus Q^{\rm gp}$ and $\varphi(a,q)=\sum_i a_it_i+f^\flat(q)\in B$, writing the group law in $B$ additively. Suppose also that $G$ is a finite rank free abelian group, $i:L\to G$ is injective, $G/i(L)$ is killed by a power of $n$, and $h:G\to B$ satisfies $hi=\varphi$ and surjects onto $B/A^\times$. Regard the integral monoid $M_{\bar x}$ as a submonoid of $B$ and define
$$P=\{g\in G:h(g)\in M_{\bar x}\}.$$
Then $P$ is fine saturated, the inclusion identifies $P^{\rm gp}$ with $G$, and there are a pointed etale neighbourhood $(W,\bar w)\to(X,\bar x)$ and a chart $P\to M|_W$ whose germ is $h|_P$, compatible with the given chart $Q\to N$ through $u:Q\to P$, $q\mapsto i(0,q)$, such that
$$W\longrightarrow Y\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[Q]}\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[P]$$
is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism, def-pc-fibre-product]. Here $\mathbf Z[T]$ is the free abelian group on symbols $z^t$, $t\in T$, with multiplication $z^tz^{t^{\prime}}=z^{t+t^{\prime}}$. The assertion concerns this prescribed inverse-image monoid and this prescribed germ, without changing the chart of $Y$.

source.place: Expose XVI Proposition 3.6.3 proof, last paragraph, printed p.252, inverse-image monoid P=h^{-1}(M_x) and etale comparison; refinement of Kato (1988) Theorem 3.5 recalled in that paragraph.

proof.text: Choose any fs chart $R\to M$ near $\bar x$ and let $F\subset R$ be the inverse image of $A^\times$. It is a face because a product in a local ring is a unit exactly when both factors are units. The chart pushout gives $M_{\bar x}=R_F\oplus_{F^{\rm gp}}A^\times$. The face-sharpening lemma therefore identifies $\overline M=M_{\bar x}/A^\times$ with the sharp fs monoid $R_F/F^{\rm gp}$ and its group completion $C=B/A^\times$ with $R^{\rm gp}/F^{\rm gp}$. In particular $C$ is finite free and $\overline M$ embeds in $C$. The same pushout shows that $M_{\bar x}$ is exactly the inverse image of $\overline M$ inside $B$: if a group element has the class of a monoid element, their difference is a unit, so it too is a monoid element.

source.place: Expose XVI Proposition 3.6.3, proof, printed p.252; explicit agent expansion of the prescribed inverse-image monoid and infinitesimal comparison argument attributed there to Kato (1988), Theorem 3.5.

proof.text: Write $\rho:G\to C$ for $h$ followed by quotient by units, and $K=\ker\rho$. Choose a basis $c_1,\ldots,c_d$ of the finite free group $C$ supplied by step 1 and lift each $c_j$ to $g_j\in G$, using the assumed surjectivity of $\rho$. Then $s(\sum a_jc_j)=\sum a_jg_j$ is a group section of $\rho$ and $G=K\oplus s(C)$. The subgroup theorem applied after a choice $G\simeq\mathbf Z^e$ makes $K$ finite free. From the inverse-image description in step 1, $P=\rho^{-1}(\overline M)=K\oplus s(\overline M)$. This equality is of actual submonoids of $G$ and keeps the specified $h$.

source.place: Expose XVI Proposition 3.6.3, proof, printed p.252; explicit agent expansion of the prescribed inverse-image monoid and infinitesimal comparison argument attributed there to Kato (1988), Theorem 3.5.

proof.text: Let $m_1,\ldots,m_v$ generate $\overline M$, and let $k_1,\ldots,k_e$ be a basis of $K$. Then $s(m_1),\ldots,s(m_v),k_1,-k_1,\ldots,k_e,-k_e$ generate $P$. It is integral as a submonoid of $G$. If $ag\in P$ with $a>0$, then $a\rho(g)\in\overline M$; saturation of $\overline M$ in $C$ implies $\rho(g)\in\overline M$ and hence $g\in P$. Finally $\overline M$ generates $C$, so $K\oplus s(\overline M)$ generates $K\oplus s(C)=G$. Thus $P$ is fs and $P^{\rm gp}\to G$ is an isomorphism induced by the inclusion. Since $hi(0,q)=f^\flat(q)\in M_{\bar x}$ for $q\in Q$, the specified $u(q)=i(0,q)$ belongs to this very $P$.

source.place: Expose XVI Proposition 3.6.3, proof, printed p.252; explicit agent expansion of the prescribed inverse-image monoid and infinitesimal comparison argument attributed there to Kato (1988), Theorem 3.5.

proof.text: The inverse image of $A^\times$ under $h|_P$ is $K$, the unit group of $P$. The map $P\oplus_K A^\times\to M_{\bar x}$, $[p,v]\mapsto h(p)v$, is surjective: lift the characteristic of a monoid element through $\rho$ and correct by a unit. It is injective as well. If $h(p)v=h(p')v'$, then $\rho(p)=\rho(p')$ so $p'=p+k$ with $k\in K$, and cancellation in $B$ gives $v=h(k)v'$. These two equalities are exactly the pushout relation $[p+k,v']=[p,h(k)v']$. Hence $h|_P$ satisfies the stalk-chart hypothesis, with its given germ, not a replacement germ.

source.place: Expose XVI Proposition 3.6.3, proof, printed p.252; explicit agent expansion of the prescribed inverse-image monoid and infinitesimal comparison argument attributed there to Kato (1988), Theorem 3.5.

proof.text: Apply stalk-chart spreading to $h|_P$, using step 3 for finite generation and integrality and step 4 for the required pushout isomorphism. It gives a pointed etale neighbourhood $W$ and a chart $P\to M|_W$ with exactly this germ. The two homomorphisms $Q\to M|_W$, one from $u$ and this chart, the other from $f^\flat$ and the fixed chart on $Y$, have equal germs. Choose a finite generating set of $Q$ and a common refinement of the finitely many pointed etale neighbourhoods on which these equalities hold. They then agree on every element of $Q$. Thus the base chart is retained. The chart ring map to functions gives a scheme map to the affine monoid spectrum by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme]. The fibre-product universal property then gives the comparison $c:W\to Z=Y\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[Q]}\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[P]$.

source.place: Expose XVI Proposition 3.6.3, proof, printed p.252; explicit agent expansion of the prescribed inverse-image monoid and infinitesimal comparison argument attributed there to Kato (1988), Theorem 3.5.

proof.text: Put $T_j$ for the log section given by $i(e_j,0)\in P$ on $W$. Its germ is $t_j$. Apply log-smooth infinitesimal calculus, including its etale-localization assertion. It gives a finite locally free logarithmic differential sheaf on $W$ and the same stalk module as in the hypothesis. Refine $W$ so that this sheaf is free. Its rank at $\bar w$ is $r$ since the specified $d\log t_j$ are a basis. In a local free frame the columns $d\log T_j$ form an $r\times r$ matrix with invertible determinant at $\bar w$; restrict to the open where this determinant is a unit, using the adjugate formula for its inverse. The $d\log T_j$ are then a basis throughout $W$. Also restrict so that $n$ is invertible, by spreading the germ of its inverse and the equation $n n^{-1}=1$. The case $r=0$ means a zero-rank sheaf and the empty matrix of determinant $1$.

source.place: Expose XVI Proposition 3.6.3, proof, printed p.252; explicit agent expansion of the prescribed inverse-image monoid and infinitesimal comparison argument attributed there to Kato (1988), Theorem 3.5.

proof.text: The underlying $W\to Y$ is locally of finite presentation by log-smooth calculus. The monoid presentation theorem gives finite generators and relations for $P$ and $Q$. Thus on an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}R\subset Y$, $Z$ is affine with algebra $D=R\otimes_{\mathbf Z[Q]}\mathbf Z[P]$ finitely presented over $R$. Indeed, maps into this affine spectrum are ring maps out of $D$, hence exactly compatible ring maps out of $R$ and $\mathbf Z[P]$; [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme] and the fibre-product universal property identify this spectrum with the indicated base change. For a finite presentation of $D$, take one variable per generator of $P$, its finitely many monoid relations as binomials, and the compatibility equations for the finitely many generators of $Q$. On any sufficiently small affine $V\subset W$ mapping there, write its algebra as $B=R[x_1,\ldots,x_a]/(f_1,\ldots,f_b)$. If $y_1,\ldots,y_c$ generate $D$ over $R$, represent each image in $B$ by $b_j(x)$. Then $B=D[x_1,\ldots,x_a]/(f_1,\ldots,f_b,y_1-b_1(x),\ldots,y_c-b_c(x))$. This explicit presentation shows $c$ is locally of finite presentation.

source.place: Expose XVI Proposition 3.6.3, proof, printed p.252; explicit agent expansion of the prescribed inverse-image monoid and infinitesimal comparison argument attributed there to Kato (1988), Theorem 3.5.

proof.text: Consider an affine square-zero test $T_0\hookrightarrow T$ for $c$, with ideal $I$, map $a_0:T_0\to W$ and prescribed map $b:T\to Z$. Give $T$ the log structure associated to the chart $P$ furnished by $b$, and $T_0$ its restriction. The general integral-chart logification lemma applies to this arbitrary scheme $T$, since $P$ is finitely generated and integral by step 3. It gives integral fine test log structures, strictness of the immersion, and the log morphism $a_0$ determined by its chart $P$. The maps to $Y$ agree through $Q$. Log-smooth calculus supplies an etale-local log lift $a:T\to W$ over $Y$. For $p\in P$, the log sections $a^\flat(p)$ and $b^\flat(p)$ agree modulo $I$. The strict-thickening fiber assertion of the logification lemma identifies the former with $b^\flat(p)(1+\epsilon(p))$ for a unique $\epsilon(p)\in I$: in the stalk pushout the fibre is the orbit of $\ker(\mathcal O_T^\times\to\mathcal O_{T_0}^\times)=1+I$, whose action is free by integrality. Multiplication and $I^2=0$ make $\epsilon:P\to I$ additive, hence extend it uniquely to $G=P^{\rm gp}$. It is zero on $i(Q^{\rm gp})$ since both maps are over $Y$.

source.place: Expose XVI Proposition 3.6.3, proof, printed p.252; explicit agent expansion of the prescribed inverse-image monoid and infinitesimal comparison argument attributed there to Kato (1988), Theorem 3.5.

proof.text: Choose the log derivation represented by the unique linear map from the pullback of $\omega_f$ to $I$ taking the basis $d\log T_j$ to $-\epsilon(i(e_j,0))$. Acting on $a$ by this derivation, as prescribed by log-smooth calculus, makes its new error $\epsilon'$ zero on $i(\mathbf Z^r\oplus Q^{\rm gp})$. Every class of $G/i(L)$ is killed by a power of $n$. Thus for each $g\in G$ some $n^k g\in i(L)$, so $n^k\epsilon'(g)=0$; multiplication by $n$ on $I$ is invertible and $\epsilon'(g)=0$. The corrected lift agrees with $b$ on $P$ and on $Y$, hence on $Z$: by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme], on monoid rings their maps agree on every basis element $z^p$, and a fibre-product map is specified by its two components. This gives etale-local lifts of the ordinary test for $c$.

source.place: Expose XVI Proposition 3.6.3, proof, printed p.252; explicit agent expansion of the prescribed inverse-image monoid and infinitesimal comparison argument attributed there to Kato (1988), Theorem 3.5.

proof.text: Any two ordinary lifts over $Z$ are log lifts over $Y$ via the same chart $P$, by the associated-log universal property. Their difference is a log derivation by log-smooth calculus. It evaluates to zero on every $d\log T_j$ since the lifts agree on $P$. These are a basis, so the derivation is zero and the lifts coincide, on every etale localization of $T$ as well. Apply the representable-presheaf sheaf theorem on $T_{\rm Et}$ to the $T$-scheme $T\times_ZW$. The etale-local lifts from step 9 agree on all overlaps by this uniqueness and glue to one lift over all of $T$. The first-order test therefore has exactly one global lift. Together with step 7, the locally-finitely-presented unique-lifting criterion proves $c$ etale. Steps 3--5 have already supplied every other conclusion and preserved the prescribed germ and base chart.

from.place: Proof Step 3: dimension-normalized Verdier duality, regular finite-torsion local model; pointwise purity and composition used to compare the normalized curve with the ambient regular scheme. Input: Gabber purity for a regular Noetherian closed pair. More precisely: Expose XVI, section 3.7 second paragraph through its last paragraph, printed pp.254--255: semistable G-alteration, ell-Sylow H, tame equivariant modification, quotient over T=S prime/H, and log resolution. Geometric construction only, before applying Theorem 3.6.2 and Proposition 3.5.7; preliminary finite extension to normalize constants in the first paragraph. Specifically: XVI 3.7, p.255: 'Le log-schema X''' est regulier et log-lisse sur T', in the uniformizer-chart form required by Theorem 3.6.2 via Proposition 3.6.3. Internal chart argument: Expose XVI Proposition 3.6.3 proof, last paragraph, printed p.252, inverse-image monoid P=h^{-1}(M_x) and etale comparison; refinement of Kato (1988) Theorem 3.5 recalled in that paragraph.

split_report.summary: Preserved the prescribed-lattice statement. Constructed P as the inverse image of the fs characteristic monoid, computed its exact stalk logification, spread the specified chart compatibly with Q, and proved the comparison etale by correcting a log-smooth infinitesimal lift using the prescribed differential basis and n-primary lattice quotient. Reused existing monoid and chart-spreading inputs. Added general log-smooth deformation calculus, the ordinary unique-lifting criterion, and integral chart logification on arbitrary schemes as statement-only nodes. The latter repairs the locally-Noetherian restriction on the existing associated-log lemma when testing arbitrary affine thickenings. Kato section 3 is WANTED, so this expanded proof is honestly marked agent-written.
split_report.blueprint: Expands the Kato-chart subargument in the Proposition 3.6.3 proof cited by the uniformizer-chart ancestry of lem-per-artin-gabber-affine-curve, proof step 3; fixed chapter and unit route retained.

Sources read: ILO XVI 3.6.2-3.6.4, printed pp.252-253; Stacks 02HG (more-morphisms.tex l.1508) and 02HM (l.1706). The item statement is unchanged and is exactly the last paragraph of ILO 3.6.3: P = h^{-1}(M_x), the prescribed germ h|_P, the fixed base chart Q and an etale comparison to Y x_{Z[Q]} Z[P]. No target is weakened and no SGA is used. Step checks: step 1 gives M_x = R_F (+)_{F^gp} A^x, the characteristic monoid R_F/F^gp by face-sharpening, and M_x as the full inverse image by integrality. In step 2, K is free and P = K (+) s(Mbar). Step 3: P is fs and P^gp = G. Step 4: P^x = K = E, and the pushout map is injective by cancellation. Step 5: the spreading hypotheses hold, and finitely many germ equalities keep the Q-chart. Step 6: the dlog basis spreads by a determinant argument and n^{-1} is spread. Step 7: I checked the presentation B = D[x]/(f, y-b(x)) is correct. Step 8: the test log structure on an arbitrary T comes from the new logification node, and the error map eps: P -> I is additive and zero on Q. Step 9: a derivation cancels eps on Z^r; eps is then zero on G because G/i(L) is n-power torsion and n is a unit on T_0. Step 10: lifts are unique because a derivation vanishing on a basis is zero; they glue on T_Et, and 02HM gives etaleness. Small cases tested: P=0 or r=0; A^1 with t=1+x; the Kummer chart N->N, 1->d, with d invertible, and its failure in characteristic p dividing d. New nodes, all true and not restatements: the log-smooth calculus is Kato 3.3/3.5/3.9/3.10. The logification node generalises lem-trf-associated-log-universal-stalks, which is locally Noetherian only and so cannot serve arbitrary affine tests; strictness and the 1+I torsor clause checked. The 02HM node is not a duplicate (lem-weil-pbc-flat-unramified-formally-etale is the converse), and Mathlib has no scheme-level FormallyEtale. No cycles. The 4 declared tool_uses are accepted as generic: face-sharpening, chart-spreading, finite monoid presentation, small-etale representable sheaf.
